sentences.t: فَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَكَ لِي
sentences.tr: fa-al-ḥamdu li-llāhi alladhī arsalaka lī
sentences.l: So praise be to God who sent you to me.
sentences.i: Praise be to God, then, who has sent you to me.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ يَا فَتَى هَلْ لَكَ فِي الشَّرَابِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat yā fatā hal laka fī al-sharāb
sentences.l: Then she said: 'O young man, is there for you in the wine?'
sentences.i: Then she said: 'O young man, would you care for wine?'

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ افْعَلِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu ifʿalī
sentences.l: So I said: 'Do it, you.'
sentences.i: And I said: 'As you wish.'
sentences.n: افْعَلِي, a feminine imperative 'do (it)', is the prince telling the princess to go ahead with what she has proposed.

sentences.t: فَعَمَدَتْ إِلَى خُرُسْتَانَ وَأَخْرَجَتْ شَرَابًا عَتِيقًا مَخْتُومًا وَنَصَبَتْ خُضْرَةً
sentences.tr: fa-ʿamadat ilā khurustāna wa-akhrajat sharāban ʿatīqan makhtūman wa-naṣabat khuḍratan
sentences.l: So she went to a store-closet, and brought out an old, sealed wine, and set up a green(-spread).
sentences.i: So she went to a small storeroom and brought out an old wine, still sealed, and spread a green cloth.
sentences.n: خُرُسْتَان is not a common word; it is taken here as naming some kind of closet or store-room (perhaps a Persian-styled compound in -stān, 'place of'), and vocalized accordingly, though the reading is a guess. خُضْرَة, 'a green (thing)', most likely names a green cloth spread for the drinking-session, though it could equally mean greens or garden produce set out with the wine; the translation follows the likelier sense.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْ وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhat wa-anshadat taqūlu shiʿr
sentences.l: Then she took (it up) and recited, saying — verse:
sentences.i: Then she took up the cup and recited, saying, in these lines:
sentences.n: شِعْرٌ stands here as the edition's own rubric introducing a verse quotation ('poetry:'), printed without a case ending tied into the sentence; it is vocalized as an independent nominative label rather than forced into agreement with تَقُولُ.

sentences.t:
لَوْ عَلِمْنَا قُدُومَكُمْ لَنَشَرْنَا مُهْجَةَ الْقَلْبِ * أَوْ سَوَادَ الْعُيُونِ
وَفَرَشْنَا خُدُودَنَا لِلِقَاكُمْ * لِيَكُونَ الْمَسِيرُ فَوْقَ الْجُفُونِ
sentences.tr:
law ʿalimnā qudūmakum la-nasharnā muhjata al-qalbi * aw sawāda al-ʿuyūni
wa-farashnā khudūdanā li-liqāʾikum * li-yakūna al-masīru fawqa al-jufūn
sentences.l: Had we known of your coming, we would have strewn the heart's life-blood, or the blackness of the eyes; and we would have spread our cheeks for meeting you, that the passage might be above the eyelids.
sentences.i: Had we but known that you were coming, we would have strewn before you the very blood of our hearts, or the dark of our eyes; we would have spread our cheeks to greet you, that your road might pass over our eyelids.
sentences.n: A conventional Nights welcome-verse: strewing the heart's blood, the dark of the eyes, or one's own cheeks and eyelashes as a carpet before an arriving guest is a stock hyperbole of hospitality and love-longing. مُهْجَة is the heart's innermost blood, the seat of life; سَوَادُ الْعُيُونِ, 'the black of the eyes', means the pupils. Being printed, pointed verse, this couplet is copied from the archive exactly as it stands and is not revocalized.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شَعْرِهَا شَكَرْتُهَا وَقَدْ تَمَكَّنَتْ مَحَبَّتُهَا وَقَدْ ذَهَبَ هَمِّي وَغَمِّي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shaʿrihā shakartuhā wa-qad tamakkanat maḥabbatuhā wa-qad dhahaba hammī wa-ghammī
sentences.l: And when she had finished with her hair, I thanked her, and her love had taken firm hold, and my care and my grief had gone.
sentences.i: When she had finished with her hair, I thanked her; her love had by now taken firm hold of me, and my care and my grief were gone.
sentences.n: شَعْر here is 'hair'; later in this same slice the identical consonants ش ع ر are vocalized شِعْر 'verse, poetry' — two different words distinguished only by the vowels we supply.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسْنَا فِي مُنَادَمَةٍ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-jalasnā fī munādamatin ilā al-layl
sentences.l: And we sat in intimate-conversation until the night.
sentences.i: And we sat together in familiar talk until nightfall.

sentences.t: فَبِتُّ مَعَهَا لَيْلَةً مَا رَأَيْتُ مِثْلَهَا فِي عُمْرِي
sentences.tr: fa-bittu maʿahā laylatan mā raʾaytu mithlahā fī ʿumrī
sentences.l: And I spent-the-night with her a night that I had not seen the like-of-it in my life.
sentences.i: And I passed the night with her — a night whose like I had never seen in all my life.
sentences.n: مَا + perfect here negates 'I had not seen', a Middle Arabic usage where Classical prose would prefer لَمْ أَرَ (compare the pilot's مَا فَارَقْتُ).

sentences.t: وَأَصْبَحْنَا نَصِلُ السُّرُورَ إِلَى وَسَطِ النَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-aṣbaḥnā naṣilu al-surūra ilā wasaṭi al-nahār
sentences.l: And we became continuing the delight until the middle of the day.
sentences.i: And we kept up our pleasure until midday.
sentences.n: أَصْبَحْنَا + a following imperfect (نَصِلُ) is one of the 'sisters of kāna': not literally 'we became' but 'we went on/carried on doing X' — here, kept the delight going.

sentences.t: فَسَكِرْتُ سُكْرًا حَتَّى غِبْتُ عَنِ الْوُجُودِ
sentences.tr: fa-sakirtu sukran ḥattā ghibtu ʿani al-wujūd
sentences.l: And I became-drunk a drunkenness, until I was-absent from existence.
sentences.i: And I grew so drunk that I lost all consciousness.
sentences.n: سُكْرًا is a cognate accusative intensifying the verb, 'a (thorough) drunkenness'. غِبْتُ عَنِ الْوُجُودِ, 'I was absent from existence', is the idiom for fainting or passing out.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ أَتَمَايَلُ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا وَ قُلْتُ لَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu atamāyalu yamīnan wa-shimālan wa-qultu lahā
sentences.l: And I rose swaying right and left, and I said to her:
sentences.i: And I got up, swaying right and left, and said to her:

sentences.t: يَا مَلِيحَةُ قُومِي أُطْلِعُكِ مِنْ تَحْتِ الْأَرْضِ وَأُرِيحُكِ مِنْ هَذَا الْجِنِّيِّ
sentences.tr: yā malīḥatu qūmī uṭliʿuki min taḥti al-arḍi wa-urīḥuki min hādhā al-jinniyy
sentences.l: O fair-one, arise! I-will-bring-you-up from beneath the earth, and I-will-relieve-you from this jinni.
sentences.i: O fair one, arise! Let me bring you up from beneath the earth and free you from this jinni.
sentences.n: أُطْلِعُكِ and أُرِيحُكِ are read as plain 1cs indicatives (the archive keeps the ي of يُرِيحُ, ruling out a jussive أُرِحْ), simple coordinated statements following the imperative rather than a subordinate result clause. مَلِيحَة is the colloquial word for 'beautiful, comely', less formal than جَمِيلَة.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَتْ وَقَالَتِ اِقْنَعْ وَاُسْكُتْ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥikat wa-qālati iqnaʿ wa-uskut
sentences.l: And she laughed and said: Be-content and be-silent!
sentences.i: And she laughed and said, 'Be content, and hold your peace!'

sentences.t: فَفِي كُلِّ عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ يَوْمٌ لِلْعِفْرِيتِ وَتِسْعَةُ أَيَّامٍ لَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-fī kulli ʿasharati ayyāmin yawmun li-al-ʿifrīti wa-tisʿatu ayyāmin laki
sentences.l: For in every ten days (there is) a day for the efrit, and nine days (are) for-you.
sentences.i: For every ten days, one day belongs to the efrit, and nine days are yours.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَكْ غَلَبَ عَلَيَّ السُّكْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lak ghalaba ʿalayya al-sukr
sentences.l: Then she said: 'to-you — the drunkenness has overcome me —
sentences.i: Then she said, 'But the drink has got the better of me —
sentences.n: لَكْ is obscure: the letters as printed give only ل ك. It may echo the لَكِ 'to/for you' two words before, or be an elliptical, dialectal لٰكِنْ 'but' marking her sudden change of heart (so taken in the idiomatic layer); it is kept here exactly as printed rather than emended.

sentences.t: أَنَا السَّاعَةَ أَكْسِرُ هَذِهِ الْقُبَّةَ الَّتِي عَلَيْهَا النَّقْشُ الْمَكْتُوبُ
sentences.tr: anā al-sāʿata aksiru hādhihi al-qubbata allatī ʿalayhā al-naqshu al-maktūb
sentences.l: I, now, shall-break this dome, upon which (is) the inscription, the written (one) —
sentences.i: I shall now break open this dome that bears the written inscription,
sentences.n: السَّاعَةَ, literally 'the hour', is an accusative of time meaning 'now, this instant'. النَّقْش الْمَكْتُوب, 'the inscription, the written one', is a pleonastic doublet: 'the written inscription'.

sentences.t: وَدَعِي الْعِفْرِيتَ يَجِيءُ حَتَّى أَقْتُلَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-daʿī al-ʿifrīta yajīʾu ḥattā aqtulahu
sentences.l: and leave the efrit — let him come — until I-kill-him —
sentences.i: and let the efrit come, that I may kill him —
sentences.n: دَعِي is the 2fs imperative 'leave, let'; the speaker (still describing her own plan) here addresses herself as one might in a burst of drunken bravado, egging herself on.

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي مُعَوَّدٌ بِقَتْلِ الْعَفَارِيتِ
sentences.tr: fa-innī muʿawwadun bi-qatli al-ʿafārīt
sentences.l: for I (am) accustomed, by the killing of efrits.
sentences.i: for I am well used to killing efrits.
sentences.n: مُعَوَّد is the masculine form of the participle, though the speaker is a woman — مُعَوَّدَة would be Classically correct; kept as printed. بِـ here marks what one is 'accustomed to' (عَوَّدَ بِـ).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامِي اِصْفَرَّتْ لَوْنُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmī iṣfarrat lawnuhā
sentences.l: And when she heard my words, her color turned-pale —
sentences.i: When she heard what I said, the color drained from her face —
sentences.n: اِصْفَرَّتْ agrees with the implied 'she' rather than with the grammatically masculine noun لَوْن ('her color turned pale' rather than the Classically expected اِصْفَرَّ لَوْنُهَا) — another loose-agreement feature of this Middle Arabic passage, alongside مُعَوَّد above.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِي بِاللَّهِ لَا تَفْعَلْ وَأَنْشَدْتُ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lī bi-Allāhi lā tafʿal wa-anshadtu
sentences.l: and she said to me: 'By God, do not do (it)!' — and I recited:
sentences.i: and said to me, 'For God's sake, do not!' — and I recited:
sentences.n: قَالَتْ and اِصْفَرَّتْ fix the speaker of 'by God, do not!' as she (the princess), addressing the narrator with the masculine imperative لَا تَفْعَلْ, correctly aimed at a male addressee. The unpointed وانشدت that follows is itself ambiguous between 3fs 'she recited' and 1cs 'I recited'; it is read here as 1cs, giving the couplet that follows — addressed, in its own grammar, to 'your' (masc.) soul — to the alarmed prince pleading with her in turn.

sentences.t: إِنَّ شَيْئًا هَلَاكُ نَفْسِكَ فِيهِ * يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَصُونَ نَفْسَكَ عَنْهُ
sentences.tr: inna shayʾan halāku nafsika fīhi * yanbaghī an taṣūna nafsaka ʿanhu
sentences.l: Indeed, a thing wherein is the destruction of your soul * it behooves that you should guard your soul against it.
sentences.i: A thing that holds within it your soul's undoing * you ought, indeed, to guard your soul against it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma anshadat taqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: Then she recited further, saying — verse:
sentences.i: Then she recited further, saying:
sentences.n: شِعْرٌ is the edition's own rubric heading the verse passage (as at the couplet just before), not a grammatical object of تَقُولُ.

sentences.t:
يَا طَالِبًا لِلْفِرَاقِ مَهْلًا * بِخَيْلِهِ سَابِقًا عِتَاقُ
اِصْبِرْ فَطَبْعُ الزَّمَانِ غَدْرٌ * وَآخِرُ الصُّحْبَةِ الْفِرَاقُ
sentences.tr:
yā ṭāliban li-al-firāqi mahlan * bi-khaylihi sābiqan ʿitāqu
iṣbir fa-ṭabʿu al-zamāni ghadrun * wa-ākhiru al-ṣuḥbati al-firāqu
sentences.l:
O you who seek separation, gently * with his outrunning steeds, thoroughbred ones.
Be patient, for the nature of time is treachery * and the end of companionship is parting.
sentences.i:
O you who race toward parting, go gently * for swift, and noble-bred, are those steeds.
Be patient, for time's very nature is treachery, * and the end of all companionship is parting.
sentences.n: خَيْل ('horses, cavalry') and عِتَاق (pl. of عَتِيق, 'thoroughbred') are collective/plural nouns of a stock image for swiftness — Parting figured as a rider on fleet, noble horses, already outrunning the one who calls after it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا وَلَمْ أَلْتَفِتْ إِلَى كَلَامِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shiʿrihā wa-lam altafit ilā kalāmihā
sentences.l: And when she had finished with her verse, and I did not turn-attention to her words —
sentences.i: When she had finished her verses, and I paid no heed to what she said —
sentences.n: التفت is spelled without the hamza its pronunciation requires (أَلْتَفِتْ, 1cs jussive after لَمْ) — the edition's ordinary habit of leaving hamza unmarked with a bare alif, as in اخيه، فان، الى (see the pilot's note). شِعْرِهَا 'her verse' is the same consonants as شَعْرِهَا 'her hair' at the opening of this slice, disambiguated only by the vowels we supply.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ رَفَعَتِ الْقُبَّةَ رَفْعًا قَوِيًّا
sentences.tr: wa-qad rafaʿati al-qubbata rafʿan qawiyyan
sentences.l: she had (already) lifted the dome, a mighty lifting.
sentences.i: she had already wrenched the dome open with mighty force.
sentences.n: قَدْ + the perfect gives pluperfect force: 'she had already…' — she was ahead of him even as he failed to attend to her. رَفْعًا قَوِيًّا is a cognate accusative of manner.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥ
sentences.l: And the dawn overtook Shahrazad, so she fell silent from the licit speech.
sentences.i: And dawn overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent, breaking off from the tale she was permitted to tell.
sentences.n: The fixed formula that closes every night of the frame story: Shahrazad's telling is only 'licit' (مُبَاح) up until daybreak, by her arrangement with the king, so dawn cuts her off here mid-story.
